methods.label: Derivative signs and continuity
methods.explanation: The derivative signs make \(f\) strictly increasing to the left of \(c\) and strictly decreasing to its right. Continuity at \(c\) joins these behaviors to the value \(f(c)\). Hence nearby values on both sides are smaller than \(f(c)\), so \(c\) is a local maximum point, C.
methods.levelReason: The reasoning uses the first-derivative sign test and the explicitly given continuity condition, within the elective scope.

needsNewNodes.name: Continuity at a point
needsNewNodes.description: A real function is continuous at a point when its nearby values approach its value there. At an interior point, both one-sided limits must equal that value. Use this condition to connect neighboring behavior to the function value at the joining point.
needsNewNodes.reason: The explanation explicitly uses point continuity. Existing catalog entries use continuity as a hypothesis or cover elementary limit calculations, but do not directly cover this general prerequisite.
